chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn at-Taymali narrated to us from his book in the month of Safar, the year 274. He said: Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir ibn Rabah al-Thaqafi narrated to us from Musa ibn Bakr, from Bashir al-Nabal. And Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaniji narrated to us from 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Bashir ibn Abi Araakah al-Nabal (and the wording of the hadith is according to the narration of Ibn 'Uqdah), saying:

When I arrived in Medina, I went to the house of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). I found his mule saddled at the door. I sat opposite the house. He came out, and I greeted him. He dismounted from the mule and came towards me. He asked: 'From where is the man?' I said: 'From Iraq.' He said: 'Which part of it?' I said: 'From the people of Kufa.' He said: 'Who accompanied you on this path?' I said: 'Some people of al-Muhaditha.' He asked: 'What is al-Muhaditha?' I said: 'Al-Murj'a.' He said: 'Woe to this al-Murj'a! To whom will they resort tomorrow when our Qa'im appears?' I said: 'They say: If that occurs, we and you will be equal in justice.' He said: 'Whoever repents, Allah accepts his repentance; and whoever conceals hypocrisy, Allah will not distance Himself from him; and whoever announces something [of hypocrisy], Allah will shed his blood.' Then he said: 'He will slaughter them, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, just as a butcher slaughters his sheep,' and he pointed to his throat with his hand.

I said: 'They say: If that occurs, his affairs will be established, and he will not shed even a drop of blood.' He said: 'No, by the One in Whose hand is my soul! It will be so until we and you wipe together sweat and blood,' and he gestured with his hand towards his forehead.

key_terms.الْبَاقِرُ: Al-Baqir (the Splitter of Knowledge), title of the fifth Imam
key_terms.الْعَرَقَ وَالْعَلَقَ: Sweat and blood, referring to the intensity of the battle
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qa'im, the Awaited Imam who will rise to establish justice
key_terms.الْقَصَّابُ: Butcher, used as a simile for the manner of slaughter
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَةُ: Al-Murj'a, a theological sect that deferred judgment on sinners

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the fate of the Murji'a before the appearance of the Qa'im?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the theological tension between the Murji'a—who deferred judgment to the future Imam—and the Imam’s assertion of immediate, decisive authority. The Imam’s gesture of wiping sweat and blood from his forehead signifies that the establishment of justice will involve both the exertion of effort and the shedding of blood, refuting the Murji'a's passive expectation of a purely peaceful transition.
